service.description: MyTime's week (mantle.work.TimesheetServices.get#PartyWeek) of the user, or of a person the user approves, with the rows added to it, each row's link; the running timer (own week); the work types offered (the services work types, design §15 Work types); the people the user may open (their own and, for an approver, the time keepers of the projects they manage; ADMIN every time keeper); and lastWeekItemCount (the items with time in the week before, for Copy last week's rows). serverNow: the server's clock, for the ticking timer.

Whether the user may log their own time on a work item: a task they may update in Projects (ironstone.TaskServices.get#TaskAccess app projects), or a project they are on (or see, as a Projects manager or ADMIN). An error otherwise.
Whether the user may change a person's entries on a day (the week's timesheet access canEdit; a future day only when the policy allows it). An error otherwise.

A grid cell: the hours of a person on a work item (or none) on a day. With no entry there one is made (from the end of the day's last entry, else 9:00), with one its hours change (zero or empty removes it), with several the day's entries are edited one by one (an error). Hours are rounded to the policy's smallest entry, at most 24.

parameter.name: billable
parameter.description: Y or N; with no entry yet, default Y

service.description: One entry in full (MyTime's EntryForm, QuickTime): a person's (default the user's) time on a work item on a day, from and thru (HH:mm) or hours from 9:00, a break, billable (Y or N), the work type and a comment; timeEntryId changes that entry. The week's access and the item are checked as for save#WeekCell.
Removes an entry of a week the user may change (not invoiced, not the running timer).

The rows added to the user's own week without time (the preference ironstone.mytime.rows.weekStart): add (workEffortId, an item the user may log on), remove (workEffortId), or copyLast (the items with time in the week before, and the rows added to it).

The work items the user logs time on, as drop-down options (value, label): with no term the open items assigned to the user, then those with the user's time in the last four weeks; with a term the open items and projects of the user's projects (or every visible one for a Projects manager) by key or name. Thirty at most.
Starts the user's timer on a work item they may log on (mantle.work.TimesheetServices.start#Timer: a timer on another item stops first).

actions.script: ec.service.sync().name('ironstone.TimeServices.check#TimeItem').parameters({workEffortId: workEffortId}).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return const out = ec.service.sync().name('mantle.work.TimesheetServices.start#Timer').parameters({workEffortId: workEffortId, comments: comments || null}).call() || {} if (ec.message.hasError()) return timeEntryId = out.timeEntryId; alreadyRunning = !!out.alreadyRunning message = out.stoppedTimeEntryIds?.length ? ec.resource.expand('Switched: the timer runs on ${workEffortId}', '', {workEffortId}) : out.message

service.description: A week's flow from MyTime and TimesheetDetail: submit (the user's own week of weekDate, or timesheetId), approve, return (reason required) or reopen (reason) of timesheetId, through mantle.work.TimesheetServices, which checks who may.
Timesheets' rows (mantle.work.TimesheetServices.find#Timesheets) with their texts and links, the counts of the chips, and the people of the find (those of the rows).

Timesheets' bulk decisions on the selected rows, each on its own (a refused one is counted, the rest go on): approve, return (reason required), or remind (the people of the rows, TimesheetServices.send#MissingTimeReminders, the week of weekDate or of each row). selectedIds: a comma list of timesheet ids, or P:partyId for a missing week.

TimesheetDetail's timesheet, for one who may view it (else "not available"): mantle.work.TimesheetServices get#TimesheetSummary with its week, the entries by day (a day's header row then its entries, each with its texts), the totals by project and item, the flags, the status history (the status audit with who and when) and the actions the user may take.

Projects Home's time: the running timer (mantle.work.TimesheetServices.get#Timer, with its item's link) and, for an approver, the submitted weeks waiting (five, oldest first; find#Timesheets toApprove).

actions.script: timer = ec.service.sync().name('mantle.work.TimesheetServices.get#Timer').call()?.timer || null if (timer?.workEffortId) timer.url = (timer.workEffortId === timer.rootWorkEffortId ? '/qapps/Projects/Projects/ProjectDetail?workEffortId=' : '/qapps/Projects/WorkItems/WorkItemDetail?workEffortId=') + encodeURIComponent(timer.workEffortId) if (timer) timer.startedText = ec.l10n.format(String(timer.fromDate), 'h:mm a') approvalList = [] if (!managers) return const rows = Array.from(ec.service.sync().name('mantle.work.TimesheetServices.find#Timesheets').parameters({list: 'toApprove', withCounts: false}) .call()?.rowList || []) rows.sort((a, b) => String(a.weekStart).localeCompare(String(b.weekStart)) || String(a.personName).localeCompare(String(b.personName))) approvalList = rows.slice(0, 5).map((row) => ({timesheetId: row.timesheetId, personName: row.personName, weekText: row.weekText, hoursText: ec.l10n.format(row.hours, '#,##0.##') + ' h', sinceText: row.submittedDate ? ec.l10n.format(String(row.submittedDate), 'MMM d') : '', url: '/qapps/Projects/Time/TimesheetDetail?timesheetId=' + encodeURIComponent(row.timesheetId)}))
